title: Reduce GPU memory & workspace usage: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, arena tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Long-context workloads and heavy KV-cache usage were triggering OOMs and unnecessarily large temporary workspace allocations on multi-GPU hosts (notably 40GB-class cards) for some production workloads. This PR combines three complementary changes to reduce peak device memory and workspace requirements: 1) integrate a lightweight activation checkpointing path for transformer blocks with optional per-layer granularity; 2) introduce pooled scratch buffers and lazy allocation for temporary kernels; 3) tune the device arena allocator with per-stream arenas and a conservative default max-resident threshold. The changes are opt-in via runtime flags and default to safe settings for existing deployments. Checklist: - [x] activation checkpointing integration and API flagging - [x] pooled scratch buffer allocator with fallback - [x] arena allocator heuristics + config - [x] kernel-selector fallback to smaller-workspace algorithms - [x] unit + perf tests added - [x] docs/release notes updated Results (internal perf bench, A100-40GB): peak device memory down ~30% on long-sequence generation (seq_len=2048, kv cache active), temporary workspace allocations down ~40%, median latency impact +2% p50, throughput stable (-3% on worst-case microbench). This reduces OOM incidents seen in ENG-9840 and enables more consistent batch packing for continuous batching in Dedicated. Related: ENG-9840, ENG-9912. Notes: activation checkpointing is conservative by default (recompute only attention MLP activations), the flag runtime.gpu.activation_checkpointing can be set per-model. Arena tuning adds runtime.gpu.arena.max_resident and runtime.gpu.arena.per_stream (true/false). Kernel selector will prefer algorithms with smaller workspace when remaining device free memory < threshold. See files changed for implementation and tests.

release_notes: Reduce GPU peak memory and temporary workspace usage by combining activation checkpointing, scratch buffer pooling, and arena allocator tuning. Opt-in checkpointing and safe defaults. Reduces OOMs for long-context workloads; minor latency tradeoff for lower memory profiles.
notes: No breaking API changes. Runtime flags allow gradual rollout. Follow-up: expose per-layer checkpointing policy in model manifest (ENG-9912).
